main_text.p: Reuertendi ætas erat, cùm annos nati essent quinquaginta. ver 25.

Cuius æquitas perpetua est, vt tantum idonei, quod ad annos & dona, ad ministerium accederent, primum ad tyrocinium obeundum, post autem ad munus plenè exequendũ; & eo probè functi, in proue-ctaætate cum vltra non possint, potestatem habe-rent & reuertendi & quiescendi. Vide in disciplina calef. supra de vocatione & filijs prophetarum.

p.i: Atq; hæc de simplicibus ordinarijs sacerdotum mu-neribus:

main_text.p: De composito verò, lex erat de summo Israeli-tarum senatu.
Sūmus senatus erat, ex sacerdotibus & Leuitis, ad controuersias arduas dirimendum. Deu. 18.8.9.10. 11. Sicut etiam ad ciuiles controuersias componen-das, Iudex summus constitutus erat.
Ad Christi autem regij muneris & sacerdotij excellentiam figurandam, postea verò in Christi aduentu abolendum, hoc constitutum erat. Zach. 12.7. 8.9.10. Collato cum figura.
Reliqui s Nazarei. sanctí sunt Mundi quicunq;
Nazarœus erat, qui votum fecerit Nazarea-tus. Num. 6.4.
Nazareatus erat votum, dese Iehoua seperando sanctitate speciali. Ibid. Amos. 2. 11. Lamént. 4.7.

page.notes: The visible part shows only the start of a large italic heading word, cut off at the right edge of the scan. The rest of the page lies outside this part. Remaining area is blank paper, with shadows of the binding along the left edge. The page is cut off at the right and at the top; the right-hand fragments of margin text are only partly legible and are not transcribed beyond the words shown. Some marginal words were not legible. Several words are uncertain, notably the Greek-free catchword area and "Specialis" at the foot.
